I've completed the web search on AI copyright legal issues in 2026, AI-generated code licensing, open source, and ethics. Here's a summary of key findings:

## Copyright and AI-Generated Code

No jurisdiction recognizes AI as a legal "person" capable of holding copyright. In the United States, copyright protection hinges on human authorship, and both case law and the U.S. Copyright Office agree that copyright protection is available only for works created through human creativity.

## Training Data and Fair Use

In the US, training on copyrighted works is likely fair use IF you obtain the copies legally, but downloading from pirate sites is not. However, major AI companies are securing content licenses rather than relying on fair use defenses.

## Open Source and AI-Generated Code

No court has yet ruled on whether training an LLM using open source code constitutes reuse or modification under open source licenses or whether doing so would violate those licenses. AI-generated code may unknowingly replicate open-source material under restrictive licenses, exposing companies to improper use or distribution liability.

## Attribution and Ethics

Attribution is a core legal and cultural norm in open source, with licenses generally requiring you to preserve copyright and authorship notices and avoid misleading claims of authorship. A growing number of open source projects are adopting disclosure rules for AI-assisted contributions.

## U.S. Copyright Office Actions

Part 2 of the Copyright Office's AI report was published on January 29, 2025, addressing the copyrightability of outputs created using generative AI, and a pre-publication version of Part 3 was released on May 9, 2025.

# Vibe Voyager — Content Gap Analysis

> Independent research conducted March 7, 2026 to identify content gaps in the existing design.

## CRITICAL GAPS (Must Add)

### 1. Karpathy's "Agentic Engineering" — The Narrative Has Evolved
**What we're missing:** Andrej Karpathy, who coined "vibe coding" in Feb 2025, declared vibe coding "passé" in Feb 2026 and introduced the term **"agentic engineering"**: orchestrating agents who write 99% of the code, with human oversight. This IS the arc of our game, but we never name it or reference this evolution.

**Impact:** This reshapes our entire narrative framing. The game's journey literally mirrors Karpathy's evolution: Vibe Coding (Act 1) → Agentic Engineering (Acts 2-3).

**Action:** Add this as a key narrative beat. When the player transitions from Act 1 to Act 2, ARIA should explicitly reference this evolution. The Debt Belt's final mission should culminate with: "Vibe coding got you here. Agentic engineering gets you to production."

**Source:** [The New Stack — Vibe Coding is Passé](https://thenewstack.io/vibe-coding-is-passe/)

---

### 2. A2A Protocol (Agent-to-Agent) — The Missing Protocol
**What we're missing:** Our content covers MCP extensively (agent-to-tool), but completely misses **A2A (Agent-to-Agent Protocol)** — Google's open protocol for agent interoperability. Launched Feb 2026, 150+ enterprise partners, now under Linux Foundation.

**The relationship:** MCP = how agents talk to tools. A2A = how agents talk to each other. Together they form the complete communication layer for multi-agent systems.

**Impact:** This is a major gap in the Orchestration Citadel content. Multi-agent orchestration is incomplete without understanding how agents discover and communicate with each other.

**Action:** Add a mission to Orchestration Citadel or create a connecting mission between MCP Station and Orchestration Citadel: "The Babel Problem" — agents can use tools (MCP) but can't talk to each other until they learn A2A.

**Source:** [Google Developers Blog — A2A](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/a2a-a-new-era-of-agent-interoperability/)

---

### 3. AI Code Quality Crisis — Specific 2026 Data
**What we're missing:** Our Debt Belt missions reference "40% vulnerable" from Forrester. The 2026 data is much more specific and alarming:
- AI code has **1.75x more logic/correctness errors**
- **2.74x more XSS vulnerabilities**
- **1.91x more insecure object references**
- **4x more code cloning** than before (developers paste more than refactor)
- Open source vulnerabilities **doubled** (107% increase in mean vulns per codebase)

**Impact:** Makes the Debt Belt missions more compelling with real data. Players should feel the urgency.

**Action:** Update Debt Belt mission content with these specific stats. The Debug challenges should reference real vulnerability types (XSS, insecure deserialization, improper password handling).

**Sources:**
- [CodeRabbit — AI vs Human Code Gen Report](https://www.coderabbit.ai/blog/state-of-ai-vs-human-code-generation-report)
- [Second Talent — AI Code Quality Metrics 2026](https://www.secondtalent.com/resources/ai-generated-code-quality-metrics-and-statistics-for-2026/)
- [Black Duck — Open Source Vulnerabilities Doubled](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/black-duck-research-shows-open-source-vulnerabilities-have-doubled-as-ai-accelerates-code-creation-302692782.html)

---

### 4. Agent SDKs — The Building Blocks
**What we're missing:** Our Framework Nebula covers CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen. But the **official vendor SDKs** for building agents are now the primary tools:
- **Claude Agent SDK** (Python + TypeScript) — same tools as Claude Code, programmable
- **OpenAI Agents SDK** — production upgrade of Swarm, with handoffs + guardrails + tracing
- **Google ADK (Agent Development Kit)** — with native A2A support

**Impact:** These are arguably more important than the third-party frameworks for a "beginner to agentic developer" journey. A student leaving this course should know how to build an agent with at least one of these SDKs.

**Action:** Add an Agent Academy mission or Academy section covering the vendor SDKs. The Framework Nebula should be expanded to include these as a fourth category: "Official SDKs" alongside the existing three frameworks.

**Sources:**
- [Claude Agent SDK Overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview)
- [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/)
- [Google ADK with A2A](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/a2a/)

---

### 5. MCP Has Evolved Significantly
**What we're missing:** Our MCP content references the initial release. MCP has evolved:
- **97 million monthly downloads** (Python + TypeScript SDKs)
- **MCP 1.0** stable spec targeting June 2026
- Now under **Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation** governance
- Claude Code 2.1 brought skill hot-reload and context fork

**Action:** Update MCP Station missions with current scale/adoption data. Mention the 1.0 spec and Linux Foundation governance in the "Protocol vs. Wrappers" mission.

**Source:** [Context Studios — MCP 1.0 and Gemini 3](https://www.contextstudios.ai/blog/ai-release-intelligence-january-2026-claude-code-21-openai-connectors-mcp-10-and-gemini-3-what-developers-need-to-know-now)

---

## IMPORTANT GAPS (Should Add)

### 6. AGENTS.md Standard
**What we're missing:** AGENTS.md is an emerging cross-tool standard for guiding coding agents, used by 60k+ open source projects, now under Linux Foundation governance. It complements CLAUDE.md (Claude-specific) with a universal format.

**Action:** Add to Academy Section 4 (Claude Code Deep Dive) or create a standalone section on "Configuring AI Agents" covering CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, and Kiro's steering docs.

**Source:** [AGENTS.md — GitHub](https://github.com/agentsmd/agents.md)

---

### 7. The Junior Developer Impact — Harvard Study
**What we're missing:** Harvard study of 62M workers: when companies adopt GenAI, **junior developer employment drops 9-10%** within six quarters, while senior employment barely budges. But AI could unlock massive demand in new domains (healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing).

**Impact:** This is critical for our audience (students). They need to understand both the threat and the opportunity. The game should address: "What does it mean for MY career?"

**Action:** Add a dialogue or mission in Act 1 (possibly a side quest on Vibe World) where a career counselor NPC discusses how the field is changing. Or address it in the text crawl / intro.

**Sources:**
- [Stack Overflow — AI vs Gen Z](https://stackoverflow.blog/2025/12/26/ai-vs-gen-z/)
- [CodeConductor — Future of Junior Developers](https://codeconductor.ai/blog/future-of-junior-developers-ai/)

---

### 8. New Roles: AI-Native Developer, AI Full-Stack Developer
**What we're missing:** New job titles have emerged:
- **AI-Native Developer** — builds with AI as default, not afterthought
- **AI Full-Stack Developer** — applications where AI is core architecture (LLMs, vector stores, agent systems in every layer)
- **Prompt Engineer** — specialist in crafting AI prompts
- **Agentic Engineer** — Karpathy's term, orchestrates AI agents

**Action:** The Academy epilogue should include a "Career Paths" section mapping game skills to real-world roles.

**Source:** [Idlen — The AI Full-Stack Developer](https://www.idlen.io/blog/ai-full-stack-developer-essential-role-2026)

---

### 9. Enterprise Adoption Stats (2026)
**What we're missing:** Hard numbers that make the content more compelling:
- **87% of Fortune 500** use at least one vibe coding tool
- **72% of enterprise AI projects** use multi-agent architectures (up from 23% in 2024)
- **150+ organizations** support the A2A protocol

**Action:** Sprinkle these stats into relevant missions as "fleet intel briefings" or dialogue callouts.

**Source:** [Second Talent — Vibe Coding Statistics](https://www.secondtalent.com/resources/vibe-coding-statistics/)

---

### 10. AI Copyright & Ethics
**What we're missing:** Legal/ethical dimensions of AI-generated code:
- No jurisdiction recognizes AI as copyright holder
- AI code may replicate open-source material under restrictive licenses
- Growing disclosure rules for AI-assisted contributions
- Training data fair use is contested

**Impact:** Any responsible curriculum should at least mention this. Security Fortress is the natural home.

**Action:** Add a side mission or dialogue in Security Fortress: "The Legal Frontier" — Mirror (the skeptic crew member) raises copyright/licensing concerns.

**Sources:**
- [U.S. Copyright Office — AI](https://www.copyright.gov/ai/)
- [Red Hat — AI and Open Source Legal Issues](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/ai-assisted-development-and-open-source-navigating-legal-issues)

---

## NICE-TO-HAVE GAPS (Consider Adding)

### 11. New Benchmarks Beyond SWE-bench
LiveCodeBench, DI-Bench, DependEval, Terminal-Bench, τ-bench (transactional tasks). The field is moving from "Can the model code?" to "Can the model engineer?"

**Action:** Brief mention in Agent Academy or Academy Resource Library.

### 12. Missing Tools in Academy
- **JetBrains AI Assistant** — built into IntelliJ ecosystem
- **Amazon Q Developer** — AWS-native, security scanning, code transformation
- **Tabnine** — privacy-focused, runs locally
- **Sourcegraph Cody** — codebase-aware AI with universal context

**Action:** Add to Academy Section 1 tool tables.

### 13. AI Testing Tools
- AI-powered visual regression testing
- AI test generation (Qodo, Diffblue)
- AI-assisted debugging (beyond code generation)

**Action:** Brief section in Academy Section 5.

---

## Summary: Design Doc Updates Required

| Gap | Priority | Location in Game | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Karpathy's "Agentic Engineering" | CRITICAL | Narrative arc, Act 1→2 transition | Reshape framing |
| A2A Protocol | CRITICAL | Orchestration Citadel (new mission) | Add mission |
| AI Code Quality 2026 data | CRITICAL | Debt Belt missions | Update stats |
| Agent SDKs (Claude/OpenAI/Google) | CRITICAL | Framework Nebula + Academy | Add coverage |
| MCP evolution (1.0, Linux Foundation) | CRITICAL | MCP Station missions | Update content |
| AGENTS.md standard | IMPORTANT | Academy Section 4 | Add section |
| Junior developer impact | IMPORTANT | Act 1 side quest or intro | Add dialogue |
| New career roles | IMPORTANT | Academy epilogue | Add section |
| Enterprise adoption stats | IMPORTANT | Various missions | Sprinkle in |
| AI copyright/ethics | IMPORTANT | Security Fortress side mission | Add dialogue |
| New benchmarks | NICE | Academy resource library | Brief mention |
| Missing tools | NICE | Academy Section 1 | Expand tables |
| AI testing tools | NICE | Academy Section 5 | Brief section |

# Vibe Voyager — Design Document

> An interactive space exploration game that teaches vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering practices. From beginner to agentic developer.

**URL:** [REDACTED_DOMAIN]
**Hosting:** Vercel (free tier)
**Target:** Lecture demo + standalone learning platform
**Deadline:** ~2026-03-14

---

## 1. Audience

Mixed levels with multiple entry points:
- Software engineering students who code but haven't used AI tools
- Working developers adopting agentic workflows
- Beginners exploring AI-assisted development
- The Academy section is accessible without playing the game (direct access for anyone)

## 2. Narrative Arc

### Act 1 — "The Solo Pilot" (Beginner)
Player wakes as a rookie developer in a single-person ship. Learns to fly by talking to ship AI (vibe coding). Fast but fragile — tech debt accumulates.

### Act 2 — "First Contact" (Intermediate)

# Vibe Voyager — Design Document

> An interactive space exploration game that teaches vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering practices. From beginner to agentic developer.

**URL:** [REDACTED_DOMAIN]
**Hosting:** Vercel (free tier)
**Target:** Lecture demo + standalone learning platform
**Deadline:** ~2026-03-14

---

## 1. Audience

Mixed levels with multiple entry points:
- Software engineering students who code but haven't used AI tools
- Working developers adopting agentic workflows
- Beginners exploring AI-assisted development
- The Academy section is accessible without playing the game (direct access for anyone)

## 2. Narrative Arc

### Act 1 — "The Solo Pilot" (Beginner)
Player wakes as a rookie developer in a single-person ship. Learns to fly by talking to ship AI (vibe coding). Fast but fragile — tech debt accumulates.

### Act 2 — "First Contact" (Intermediate)
Discovers MCP — a universal docking protocol. Learns agent architecture (Perceive → Plan → Act → Reflect). Recruits first crew members (autonomous agents).

### Act 3 — "Fleet Commander" (Advanced)
Commands a fleet of specialized agent ships (multi-agent orchestration). Faces the Integration Nebula, deploys HITL safety systems, handles security threats. Final boss: deploying a production-grade agentic system.

### Epilogue — "The Academy" (Practitioner)
Ship docks at Fleet HQ. Unlocks real-world tooling guides. Space aesthetic continues, real-world content inside. Also accessible from title screen without game progress.

## 3. Tech Stack

| Dependency | Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Next.js | 15 (stable) | App Router, SSR/SSG, routing |
| TypeScript | latest | Type safety |
| Tailwind CSS | v4 | CSS-first config via `@import "tailwindcss"` and `@theme` |
| Motion | latest | Animations (`motion/react`, NOT framer-motion) |
| HTML5 Canvas | native | Star map, mini-games |
| Howler.js | latest | Audio (ambient loops + SFX sprites, 7kb gzipped) |
| localStorage | native | Game save state (no backend) |
| Vercel | free tier | Hosting + custom domain |

**No backend, no database, no auth.** All state client-side.

### Typography
- Display: Space Grotesk
- Body: Inter
- Mono: JetBrains Mono

### Color System
| Token | Hex | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| Void | `#0a0f1a` | Deep space background |
| Nebula Blue | `#4a6fa5` | Primary UI, MCP content |
| Signal Green | `#6b9e78` | Success, agent content, Plan/Act |
| Core Terracotta | `#c17147` | Warnings, highlights, player actions |
| Starlight | `#e8e0d4` | Text, glowing elements |
| Glass | `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)` | Glassmorphism panels with backdrop-blur |

### Visual Style
Clean minimalist sci-fi. Glassmorphism panels, parallax starfields, SVG planets with orbital rings, spring-physics animations, subtle glow effects. Think *Interstellar* UI meets Linear's design language.

### Audio
Full soundscape: ambient space synth loop + UI SFX (button clicks, warp sounds, mission complete chimes, dialogue bleeps). Synthwave style. Audio opt-in on first interaction (browser requirement).

## 4. Project Structure

```
app/
├── page.tsx                    # Title screen (New Game / Continue / Academy / About)
├── create/                     # Character creation (3 steps)
├── cockpit/                    # Ship HUD — main dashboard
├── starmap/                    # Interactive galaxy map (Canvas)
├── planets/
│   ├── vibe-world/            # Act 1: Vibe coding fundamentals
│   ├── debt-belt/             # Act 1: Tech debt dangers
│   ├── mcp-station/           # Act 2: Model Context Protocol
│   ├── agent-academy/         # Act 2: Agent architecture
│   ├── framework-nebula/      # Act 2: LangGraph vs CrewAI vs AutoGen
│   ├── orchestration-citadel/ # Act 3: Multi-agent systems
│   ├── security-fortress/     # Act 3: HITL, local LLMs, security
│   └── production-worlds/     # Act 3: Enterprise deployment
├── academy/                    # Epilogue: Real-world tooling guides
├── inventory/                  # Collected tools/items
└── crew/                       # Recruited agent crew

components/
├── game/
│   ├── StarMap.tsx             # Canvas-based galaxy navigation
│   ├── Cockpit.tsx             # HUD with stats, fuel, crew
│   ├── DialogueSystem.tsx      # NPC conversation engine
│   ├── MissionBriefing.tsx     # Mission intro/outro screens
│   ├── MiniGame.tsx            # Base mini-game wrapper
│   └── Inventory.tsx           # Item management UI
├── ui/
│   ├── GlassPanel.tsx          # Glassmorphism container
│   ├── XPBar.tsx               # Experience progress bar
│   ├── StatGauge.tsx           # Radial stat display
│   ├── TypewriterText.tsx      # Animated text reveal
│   └── WarpTransition.tsx      # Page transition effect
├── audio/
│   └── AudioManager.tsx        # Howler.js wrapper, SFX triggers

lib/
├── game-state.ts               # Save/load, progression logic
├── missions.ts                 # Mission definitions & requirements
├── dialogue-data.ts            # NPC conversation trees
├── items.ts                    # Item/tool definitions
└── crew.ts                     # Crew member definitions & stats

public/
├── audio/
│   ├── ambient-space.mp3
│   └── sfx/                    # UI sounds
├── images/
│   ├── planets/                # SVG/PNG planet illustrations
│   ├── characters/             # NPC portraits
│   ├── items/                  # Inventory icons
│   └── backgrounds/            # Starfields, nebulae
```

## 5. Game Systems

### Player Stats (4 stats, each 1–10)
| Stat | Represents | Leveled by |
|---|---|---|
| Vibe | Natural language fluency with AI | Vibe coding missions, prompt challenges |
| Architecture | System design & agent thinking | Agent anatomy, framework comparisons |
| Protocol | Integration & MCP knowledge | MCP missions, connection challenges |
| Command | Leadership of multi-agent systems | Orchestration missions, fleet exercises |

### Ranks (combined stat total)
| Rank | Total | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| Cadet | 4–10 | Act 1 |
| Navigator | 11–20 | Act 2 |
| Commander | 21–30 | Act 3 |
| Admiral | 31–40 | Academy (also accessible from title screen) |

### Character Creation
1. Choose callsign (text input)
2. Choose ship (3 cosmetic SVG silhouettes: The Spark, The Architect, The Sentinel)
3. Intro text crawl → [ LAUNCH ] → warp into cockpit

### Mission Structure
Each planet has 3–5 missions. Each mission follows: **Briefing → Learning Phase → Challenge → Debrief**

### Challenge Types
| Type | Mechanic |
|---|---|
| Prompt Duel | Write best natural language prompt, scored on completeness |
| Architect | Drag-and-drop nodes to build system diagrams |
| Connect | Draw connections in visual puzzle (MCP wiring) |
| Debug | Find problems in code/architecture scenarios |
| Command | Assign right agents to right tasks |
| Dialogue | NPC quiz-conversations with branching answers |

### Crew System (maps to Perceive → Plan → Act → Reflect)
| Member | Role | Recruited at |
|---|---|---|
| ARIA | Ship AI / narrator | Start of game |
| Scout | Perception specialist | Agent Academy M1 |
| Archie | Planning / reasoning | Agent Academy M3 |
| Exec | Action / execution | Agent Academy M5 |
| Mirror | Reflection / testing | Security Fortress M1 |

### Inventory
Items = real tools with in-game names. Each has a description card explaining the real-world tool.
- Ship Voice Module (Claude Code / Cursor)
- Context Adapter (MCP)
- Agent Blueprint (Agent architecture pattern)
- Fleet Comm Array (Multi-agent orchestration)
- Security Shield (HITL framework)
- Local Core (Ollama / Local LLMs)
- Skill Chips (Claude Code skills/plugins)

### Save System
- Auto-save to localStorage after every mission
- No password gating — progression earned through completion
- "New Game" reset option

## 6. Planet-by-Planet Content Map

### ACT 1 — "The Solo Pilot"

**Vibe World** (4 missions)
1. "First Words" — What is vibe coding → Dialogue quiz (sources: IBM, Replit, Wikipedia, Google Cloud)
2. "See It, Say It, Run It" — First vibe creation → Prompt Duel (sources: Slide 2, Beginner Guide)
3. "The Prototype Sprint" — Build fast → Timed challenge (source: arXiv Vibe Coding in Practice)
4. "Traditional vs. Vibe" — Both paradigms → Debate dialogue (source: arXiv GenAI & Software Dev)

**Debt Asteroid Belt** (3 missions)
1. "The Fragile Ship" — Tech debt → Debug 5 problems (sources: Slide 9, Tabnine)
2. "40% Vulnerable" — Security audit → Bin-sorting mini-game (source: arXiv, Security Auto Fixer)
3. "The Case for Expertise" — Why vibe alone fails → Dialogue quiz, unlocks Act 2

### ACT 2 — "First Contact"

**MCP Station** (4 missions)
1. "The N×M Problem" — Integration bottleneck → Visual puzzle (source: Slide 4)
2. "USB-C for AI" — What MCP is → Connect puzzle (sources: Slide 5, Anthropic, IBM)
3. "Protocol vs. Wrappers" — Comparison → Dialogue quiz (source: Slide 6)
4. "Docking Sequence" — MCP hands-on → Architect JSON blocks (source: Anthropic docs)

**Agent Academy** (5 missions)
1. "The Cognitive Loop" — Agent anatomy → Architect cycle + recruit Scout (source: Slide 3)
2. "Perception Training" — How agents see → Sorting mini-game (source: arXiv)
3. "Planning & Reasoning" — Chain of thought → Tree decomposition + recruit Archie (source: Deep Agent article)
4. "Tool Calling" — How agents act → Connect puzzle (sources: Akka, ACI)
5. "Self-Healing" — Reflect loop → Debug scenarios + recruit Exec (source: Slide 3)

**Framework Nebula** (3 missions)
1. "Three Schools of Thought" — Framework overview → NPC dialogues (source: Slide 8, DataCamp)
2. "The Right Tool" — When to use what → Command matching (source: DataCamp)
3. "Build a Crew" — CrewAI concepts → Architect fill-in-blank (sources: CrewAI, CAMEL repos)

### ACT 3 — "Fleet Commander"

**Orchestration Citadel** (3 missions)
1. "Society of Agents" — Multi-agent pipeline → Architect nodes (source: Slide 7)
2. "Message Passing" — Agent communication → Connect routing (sources: arXiv, Devin blog)
3. "Delegation" — What to automate → Command triage (source: arXiv)

**Security Fortress** (3 missions)
1. "The Safety Net" — HITL → Architect flowchart + recruit Mirror (sources: Slide 10, Galileo)
2. "Local Defenses" — Local LLMs → Dialogue quiz (source: Slide 11)
3. "Threat Scan" — Security vulnerabilities → Debug challenge (sources: Auto Fixer, CWE-95)

**Production Worlds** (3 missions — three moons)
1. "Moon Alpha: Quality Engineering" — Self-healing tests → Command (sources: Slide 12, SWE-bench)
2. "Moon Beta: The Enterprise" — Real-world cases → Dialogue quiz (source: Slides 12-13)
3. "Final Mission: Deployment Playbook" — Capstone → Multi-step Architect (sources: Slides 14-15)

## 7. The Academy (Epilogue + Direct Access)

Accessible from title screen without game progress. Space aesthetic continues, real-world content inside glassmorphism panels with terminal-style code blocks.

### Section 1: AI-Powered IDEs & Editors

#### GUI-Based IDEs
| Tool | Developer | Key Differentiator | Pricing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cursor** | Anysphere | Largest community, highest benchmark scores, tab completions + agent mode | $20/mo Pro |
| **Google Antigravity** | Google | Agent-first platform, Manager Surface for multi-agent orchestration, built-in browser testing | Free preview |
| **Kiro** | AWS | Spec-driven development, Agent Hooks for automation, Agent Steering docs | Free preview |
| **Windsurf** | Cognition (Devin) | Cascade agent anticipates next moves, best value at $15/mo | $15/mo Pro |
| **GitHub Copilot** | GitHub/Microsoft | Deepest GitHub integration, workspace agents, code review built-in | $10/mo |

#### Terminal-Native Agents
| Tool | Developer | Key Differentiator | Pricing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code** | Anthropic | 1M token context, deepest reasoning, skills/plugins/hooks ecosystem | $20/mo Pro, $100-200/mo Teams |
| **Codex CLI** | OpenAI | Rust-built, multi-agent with worktrees, MCP support, open source | Usage-based |
| **Gemini CLI** | Google | 1M token context, free tier (60 req/min), Google Search grounding, open source (Apache 2.0) | Free / usage-based |
| **Aider** | Paul Gauthier | Speed-focused, multi-file changes via natural language, git-aware, open source | Free (OSS) |

#### VS Code Extensions (Open Source)
| Tool | Key Differentiator |
|---|---|
| **Cline** | Model-agnostic, stepwise Plan→Act pipeline, full audit trail, governance-focused |
| **Roo Code** | Cline fork, role-driven execution modes (architect/tester), faster on large multi-file changes |
| **Continue** | Open-source autopilot, source-controlled AI checks on PRs |

### Section 2: AI Code Review & Quality Tools

| Tool | What It Does |
|---|---|
| **CodeRabbit** | AI PR reviewer on GitHub/GitLab, 2M+ repos connected, auto-summaries and walkthroughs |
| **Greptile** | Full-codebase graph analysis for cross-file bug detection |
| **Qodo** | Behavior-focused review, auto-generates test suites, persistent codebase intelligence |
| **Ellipsis** | Auto-generates fixes for reviewer comments, reduces review cycles |
| **Cursor BugBot** | Automated bug detection integrated into Cursor IDE |

### Section 3: No-Code / Low-Code Builders

| Tool | What It Does |
|---|---|
| **Replit** | Browser-based IDE with AI agent, deploy in one click |
| **Bolt.new** | Prompt-to-app builder, full-stack in browser |
| **Lovable** | AI app builder focused on design quality |
| **v0 by Vercel** | UI component generator from prompts, React + Tailwind output |

### Section 4: Claude Code Deep Dive
- Installation & setup
- CLAUDE.md configuration (global vs. project vs. local)
- Skills: what they are, how to create and use them
- Plugins: installing from marketplaces, compound-engineering, superpowers
- Hooks: pre/post tool call automation
- Agent teams: parallel execution with subagents
- Keybindings & keyboard shortcuts
- MCP server configuration
- Best practices: brainstorming → planning → execution → review cycle

### Section 5: Agentic Development Best Practices
- Subagent-driven development (5-step workflow)
- When to parallelize vs. serialize
- Code review with AI (using multiple reviewer agents)
- Test-driven development with agents
- Memory management (CLAUDE.md, memory files, progressive disclosure)
- Security: HITL patterns, sandboxing, local LLMs
- Prompt engineering for code generation
- Managing technical debt in AI-assisted codebases

### Section 6: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Workshop
- What MCP is and why it matters (from game content, reinforced with hands-on)
- Setting up MCP servers (stdio vs. HTTP)
- Connecting Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI to MCP
- Building your own MCP server
- MCP in enterprise: governance and scaling

### Section 7: Resource Library
All 57+ sources from sources.md, organized by topic with description cards.
Links to arXiv papers, corporate articles, GitHub repos, benchmarks.

### Section 8: How This Was Built
Meta case study from BUILD_LOG.md:
- The brainstorming process
- Planning with skills
- Parallel agent execution (what ran concurrently)
- Plugins & skills used
- Metrics (lines of code, time, agent count)
- Lessons learned

## 8. UX Flow

### Title Screen
Slow-drifting parallax starfield. Nebula gradient pulses gently.

```
         V I B E   V O Y A G E R
         The Agentic Coding Odyssey

         [  N E W   G A M E  ]
         [  C O N T I N U E  ]
         [  A C A D E M Y    ]
         [  A B O U T        ]
```

- Ambient audio starts on first interaction
- "Continue" grayed out if no save exists
- "Academy" always accessible (no game progress required)

### Core Navigation Loop
```
Star Map ──select planet──→ Planet (missions) ──complete/return──→ Cockpit (HUD home)
   ↑                                                                      │
   └──────────────────────── open star map ───────────────────────────────┘
```

### Persistent Nav Bar (bottom, cockpit-styled)
Star Map | Cockpit (home) | Crew | Inventory | Academy | Audio Toggle

### Star Map (Canvas)
- 3-layer parallax starfield
- Planets as glowing spheres with orbital ring animations
- 3 visible regions: Act 1 (warm, center), Act 2 (cool, frontier), Act 3 (dramatic, edge)
- Academy space station always visible at top
- Planet states: Locked (dim) → Available (pulsing) → In Progress (partial ring) → Completed (full glow + badge)

### Cockpit HUD
Glassmorphism panels on starfield:
- Callsign + Rank
- 4 stat gauges (radial/horizontal bars with glow)
- Crew portraits (silhouette with "?" for unrecruited)
- Mission log (current objective + overall progress)
- Recent inventory items

### Page Transitions
- Star Map → Planet: Stars streak toward center (warp in)
- Planet → Cockpit: Gentle fade with HUD boot-up flicker
- Cockpit → Star Map: Reverse warp (stars expand outward)
- Mission complete: Flash of light → debrief slides in
- All via Motion `AnimatePresence` with custom variants

### Mobile Responsiveness
- Star map: scrollable/zoomable touch canvas
- Cockpit: stacks vertically
- Dialogue: already mobile-friendly (text + buttons)
- Mini-games: tap instead of click/drag
- Nav bar: fixed bottom (thumb-friendly)

## 9. Content Gaps to Create

| Gap | Location | Source |
|---|---|---|
| AI tools landscape (IDEs, agents, review tools) | Academy Sections 1-3 | Research + first-hand experience |
| Claude Code deep dive tutorials | Academy Section 4 | Written from experience |
| Agentic best practices guide | Academy Section 5 | [redacted-project]/Continuum workflows |
| MCP setup walkthrough | Academy Section 6 | Anthropic docs |
| Mini-game interactive content | All challenge missions | Built as game mechanics |
| NPC dialogue scripts | All planets | Written from source material |
| Audio assets | Global | Royalty-free / generated |
| Planet/character SVG illustrations | Global | AI-generated or designed |

## 10. Build Approach

- **Framework:** Superpowers plugin workflow (brainstorm → plan → execute → review)
- **Execution:** Subagent-driven development with parallel agent teams
- **Quality:** Compound engineering review agents between phases
- **Tracking:** BUILD_LOG.md updated after every major milestone
- **Verification:** verification-before-completion skill before any "done" claim
- **Docs:** Context7 for all library API verification before writing code

---

*Design approved 2026-03-07. Ready for implementation planning.*

Confronts real 2026 data: AI code has 1.75x more bugs, 2.74x more XSS vulnerabilities. ARIA's key lesson: "Vibe coding got you here. Agentic engineering gets you to production."

### Act 2 — "First Contact" (Intermediate) — Agentic Engineering
Discovers MCP (agent-to-tool) and A2A (agent-to-agent) — the twin communication protocols. Learns agent architecture (Perceive → Plan → Act → Reflect). Recruits first crew members. Explores both third-party frameworks (CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen) AND official Agent SDKs (Claude, OpenAI, Google ADK).

### Act 3 — "Fleet Commander" (Advanced) — Production Mastery
Commands a fleet of specialized agent ships (multi-agent orchestration via A2A). Faces the Integration Nebula, deploys HITL safety systems, handles security threats including AI copyright/ethics. Final boss: deploying a production-grade agentic system.

### Epilogue — "The Academy" (Practitioner)
Ship docks at Fleet HQ. Unlocks real-world tooling guides. Space aesthetic continues, real-world content inside. Also accessible from title screen without game progress.

# Vibe Voyager — Design Document

> An interactive space exploration game that teaches vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering practices. From beginner to agentic developer.

**URL:** [REDACTED_DOMAIN]

## 1. Audience

Mixed levels with multiple entry points:
- Software engineering students who code but haven't used AI tools
- Working developers adopting agentic workflows
- Beginners exploring AI-assisted development
- The Academy section is accessible without playing the game (direct access for anyone)

## 2. Narrative Arc

**Key narrative thread:** The game mirrors Karpathy's own evolution — he coined "vibe coding" (Feb 2025), then declared it "passé" and introduced **"agentic engineering"** (Feb 2026). The player lives this arc.

### Act 1 — "The Solo Pilot" (Beginner) — Vibe Coding
Player wakes as a rookie developer in a single-person ship. Learns to fly by talking to ship AI (vibe coding). Fast but fragile — tech debt accumulates. Confronts real 2026 data: AI code has 1.75x more bugs, 2.74x more XSS vulnerabilities. ARIA's key lesson: "Vibe coding got you here. Agentic engineering gets you to production."

### Act 2 — "First Contact" (Intermediate) — Agentic Engineering
Discovers MCP (agent-to-tool) and A2A (agent-to-agent) — the twin communication protocols. Learns agent architecture (Perceive → Plan → Act → Reflect). Recruits first crew members. Explores both third-party frameworks (CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen) AND official Agent SDKs (Claude, OpenAI, Google ADK).

### Act 3 — "Fleet Commander" (Advanced) — Production Mastery
Commands a fleet of specialized agent ships (multi-agent orchestration via A2A). Faces the Integration Nebula, deploys HITL safety systems, handles security threats including AI copyright/ethics. Final boss: deploying a production-grade agentic system.

### Epilogue — "The Academy" (Practitioner)

Slow-drifting parallax starfield. Nebula gradient pulses gently.

         [  C O N T I N U E  ]
         [  A C A D E M Y    ]

```

- Ambient audio starts on first interaction
- "Continue" grayed out if no save exists
- "Academy" always accessible (no game progress required)

### Core Navigation Loop
```
Star Map ──select planet──→ Planet (missions) ──complete/return──→ Cockpit (HUD home)
   ↑                                                                      │
   └──────────────────────── open star map ───────────────────────────────┘
```

Star Map | Cockpit (home) | Crew | Inventory | Academy | Audio Toggle

### Star Map (Canvas)
- 3-layer parallax starfield
- Planets as glowing spheres with orbital ring animations
- 3 visible regions: Act 1 (warm, center), Act 2 (cool, frontier), Act 3 (dramatic, edge)
- Academy space station always visible at top
- Planet states: Locked (dim) → Available (pulsing) → In Progress (partial ring) → Completed (full glow + badge)

### Cockpit HUD
Glassmorphism panels on starfield:
- Callsign + Rank
- 4 stat gauges (radial/horizontal bars with glow)
- Crew portraits (silhouette with "?" for unrecruited)
- Mission log (current objective + overall progress)
- Recent inventory items

### Page Transitions
- Star Map → Planet: Stars streak toward center (warp in)
- Planet → Cockpit: Gentle fade with HUD boot-up flicker
- Cockpit → Star Map: Reverse warp (stars expand outward)

- Star map: scrollable/zoomable touch canvas
- Cockpit: stacks vertically
- Dialogue: already mobile-friendly (text + buttons)
- Mini-games: tap instead of click/drag
- Nav bar: fixed bottom (thumb-friendly)

# Vibe Voyager — Design Document

> An interactive space exploration game that teaches vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering practices. From beginner to agentic developer.

**URL:** [REDACTED_DOMAIN]
**Hosting:** Vercel (free tier)
**Target:** Lecture demo + standalone learning platform
**Deadline:** ~2026-03-14

---

## 1. Audience

Mixed levels with multiple entry points:
- Software engineering students who code but haven't used AI tools
- Working developers adopting agentic workflows
- Beginners exploring AI-assisted development
- The Academy section is accessible without playing the game (direct access for anyone)

## 2. Narrative Arc

**Key narrative thread:** The game mirrors Karpathy's own evolution — he coined "vibe coding" (Feb 2025), then declared it "passé" and introduced **"agentic engineering"** (Feb 2026). The player lives this arc.

### Act 1 — "The Solo Pilot" (Beginner) — Vibe Coding
Player wakes as a rookie developer in a single-person ship. Learns to fly by talking to ship AI (vibe coding). Fast but fragile — tech debt accumulates. Confronts real 2026 data: AI code has 1.75x more bugs, 2.74x more XSS vulnerabilities. ARIA's key lesson: "Vibe coding got you here. Agentic engineering gets you to production."

### Act 2 — "First Contact" (Intermediate) — Agentic Engineering
Discovers MCP (agent-to-tool) and A2A (agent-to-agent) — the twin communication protocols. Learns agent architecture (Perceive → Plan → Act → Reflect). Recruits first crew members. Explores both third-party frameworks (CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen) AND official Agent SDKs (Claude, OpenAI, Google ADK).

### Act 3 — "Fleet Commander" (Advanced) — Production Mastery
Commands a fleet of specialized agent ships (multi-agent orchestration via A2A). Faces the Integration Nebula, deploys HITL safety systems, handles security threats including AI copyright/ethics. Final boss: deploying a production-grade agentic system.

### Epilogue — "The Academy" (Practitioner)
Ship docks at Fleet HQ. Unlocks real-world tooling guides. Space aesthetic continues, real-world content inside. Also accessible from title screen without game progress.

## 3. Tech Stack

| Dependency | Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Next.js | 15 (stable) | App Router, SSR/SSG, routing |
| TypeScript | latest | Type safety |
| Tailwind CSS | v4 | CSS-first config via `@import "tailwindcss"` and `@theme` |
| Motion | latest | Animations (`motion/react`, NOT framer-motion) |
| HTML5 Canvas | native | Star map, mini-games |
| Howler.js | latest | Audio (ambient loops + SFX sprites, 7kb gzipped) |
| localStorage | native | Game save state (no backend) |
| Vercel | free tier | Hosting + custom domain |

**No backend, no database, no auth.** All state client-side.

### Typography
- Display: Space Grotesk
- Body: Inter
- Mono: JetBrains Mono

### Color System
| Token | Hex | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| Void | `#0a0f1a` | Deep space background |
| Nebula Blue | `#4a6fa5` | Primary UI, MCP content |
| Signal Green | `#6b9e78` | Success, agent content, Plan/Act |
| Core Terracotta | `#c17147` | Warnings, highlights, player actions |
| Starlight | `#e8e0d4` | Text, glowing elements |
| Glass | `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)` | Glassmorphism panels with backdrop-blur |

### Visual Style
Clean minimalist sci-fi. Glassmorphism panels, parallax starfields, SVG planets with orbital rings, spring-physics animations, subtle glow effects. Think *Interstellar* UI meets Linear's design language.

### Audio
Full soundscape: ambient space synth loop + UI SFX (button clicks, warp sounds, mission complete chimes, dialogue bleeps). Synthwave style. Audio opt-in on first interaction (browser requirement).

# Vibe Voyager — Design Document

> An interactive space exploration game that teaches vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering practices. From beginner to agentic developer.

**URL:** [REDACTED_DOMAIN]
**Hosting:** Vercel (free tier)
**Target:** Lecture demo + standalone learning platform
**Deadline:** ~2026-03-14

---

## 1. Audience

Mixed levels with multiple entry points:
- Software engineering students who code but haven't used AI tools
- Working developers adopting agentic workflows
- Beginners exploring AI-assisted development
- The Academy section is accessible without playing the game (direct access for anyone)

## 2. Narrative Arc

**Key narrative thread:** The game mirrors Karpathy's own evolution — he coined "vibe coding" (Feb 2025), then declared it "passé" and introduced **"agentic engineering"** (Feb 2026). The player lives this arc.

### Act 1 — "The Solo Pilot" (Beginner) — Vibe Coding
Player wakes as a rookie developer in a single-person ship. Learns to fly by talking to ship AI (vibe coding). Fast but fragile — tech debt accumulates. Confronts real 2026 data: AI code has 1.75x more bugs, 2.74x more XSS vulnerabilities. ARIA's key lesson: "Vibe coding got you here. Agentic engineering gets you to production."

### Act 2 — "First Contact" (Intermediate) — Agentic Engineering
Discovers MCP (agent-to-tool) and A2A (agent-to-agent) — the twin communication protocols. Learns agent architecture (Perceive → Plan → Act → Reflect). Recruits first crew members. Explores both third-party frameworks (CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen) AND official Agent SDKs (Claude, OpenAI, Google ADK).

### Act 3 — "Fleet Commander" (Advanced) — Production Mastery
Commands a fleet of specialized agent ships (multi-agent orchestration via A2A). Faces the Integration Nebula, deploys HITL safety systems, handles security threats including AI copyright/ethics. Final boss: deploying a production-grade agentic system.

### Epilogue — "The Academy" (Practitioner)
Ship docks at Fleet HQ. Unlocks real-world tooling guides. Space aesthetic continues, real-world content inside. Also accessible from title screen without game progress.

## 3. Tech Stack

| Dependency | Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Next.js | 15 (stable) | App Router, SSR/SSG, routing |
| TypeScript | latest | Type safety |
| Tailwind CSS | v4 | CSS-first config via `@import "tailwindcss"` and `@theme` |
| Motion | latest | Animations (`motion/react`, NOT framer-motion) |
| HTML5 Canvas | native | Star map, mini-games |
| Howler.js | latest | Audio (ambient loops + SFX sprites, 7kb gzipped) |
| localStorage | native | Game save state (no backend) |
| Vercel | free tier | Hosting + custom domain |

**No backend, no database, no auth.** All state client-side.

### Typography
- Display: Space Grotesk
- Body: Inter
- Mono: JetBrains Mono

### Color System
| Token | Hex | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| Void | `#0a0f1a` | Deep space background |
| Nebula Blue | `#4a6fa5` | Primary UI, MCP content |
| Signal Green | `#6b9e78` | Success, agent content, Plan/Act |
| Core Terracotta | `#c17147` | Warnings, highlights, player actions |
| Starlight | `#e8e0d4` | Text, glowing elements |
| Glass | `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)` | Glassmorphism panels with backdrop-blur |

### Visual Style
Clean minimalist sci-fi. Glassmorphism panels, parallax starfields, SVG planets with orbital rings, spring-physics animations, subtle glow effects. Think *Interstellar* UI meets Linear's design language.

### Audio
Full soundscape: ambient space synth loop + UI SFX (button clicks, warp sounds, mission complete chimes, dialogue bleeps). Synthwave style. Audio opt-in on first interaction (browser requirement).

## 4. Project Structure

# Vibe Voyager — Design Document

> An interactive space exploration game that teaches vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering practices. From beginner to agentic developer.

**URL:** [REDACTED_DOMAIN]
**Hosting:** Vercel (free tier)
**Target:** Lecture demo + standalone learning platform
**Deadline:** ~2026-03-14

---

## 1. Audience

Mixed levels with multiple entry points:
- Software engineering students who code but haven't used AI tools
- Working developers adopting agentic workflows
- Beginners exploring AI-assisted development
- The Academy section is accessible without playing the game (direct access for anyone)

## 2. Narrative Arc

**Key narrative thread:** The game mirrors Karpathy's own evolution — he coined "vibe coding" (Feb 2025), then declared it "passé" and introduced **"agentic engineering"** (Feb 2026). The player lives this arc.

### Act 1 — "The Solo Pilot" (Beginner) — Vibe Coding
Player wakes as a rookie developer in a single-person ship. Learns to fly by talking to ship AI (vibe coding). Fast but fragile — tech debt accumulates. Confronts real 2026 data: AI code has 1.75x more bugs, 2.74x more XSS vulnerabilities. ARIA's key lesson: "Vibe coding got you here. Agentic engineering gets you to production."

### Act 2 — "First Contact" (Intermediate) — Agentic Engineering
Discovers MCP (agent-to-tool) and A2A (agent-to-agent) — the twin communication protocols. Learns agent architecture (Perceive → Plan → Act → Reflect). Recruits first crew members. Explores both third-party frameworks (CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen) AND official Agent SDKs (Claude, OpenAI, Google ADK).

### Act 3 — "Fleet Commander" (Advanced) — Production Mastery
Commands a fleet of specialized agent ships (multi-agent orchestration via A2A). Faces the Integration Nebula, deploys HITL safety systems, handles security threats including AI copyright/ethics. Final boss: deploying a production-grade agentic system.

### Epilogue — "The Academy" (Practitioner)
Ship docks at Fleet HQ. Unlocks real-world tooling guides. Space aesthetic continues, real-world content inside. Also accessible from title screen without game progress.

## 3. Tech Stack

| Dependency | Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Next.js | 15 (stable) | App Router, SSR/SSG, routing |
| TypeScript | latest | Type safety |
| Tailwind CSS | v4 | CSS-first config via `@import "tailwindcss"` and `@theme` |
| Motion | latest | Animations (`motion/react`, NOT framer-motion) |
| HTML5 Canvas | native | Star map, mini-games |
| Howler.js | latest | Audio (ambient loops + SFX sprites, 7kb gzipped) |
| localStorage | native | Game save state (no backend) |
| Vercel | free tier | Hosting + custom domain |

**No backend, no database, no auth.** All state client-side.

### Typography
- Display: Space Grotesk
- Body: Inter
- Mono: JetBrains Mono

### Color System
| Token | Hex | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| Void | `#0a0f1a` | Deep space background |
| Nebula Blue | `#4a6fa5` | Primary UI, MCP content |
| Signal Green | `#6b9e78` | Success, agent content, Plan/Act |
| Core Terracotta | `#c17147` | Warnings, highlights, player actions |
| Starlight | `#e8e0d4` | Text, glowing elements |
| Glass | `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)` | Glassmorphism panels with backdrop-blur |

### Visual Style
Clean minimalist sci-fi. Glassmorphism panels, parallax starfields, SVG planets with orbital rings, spring-physics animations, subtle glow effects. Think *Interstellar* UI meets Linear's design language.

### Audio
Full soundscape: ambient space synth loop + UI SFX (button clicks, warp sounds, mission complete chimes, dialogue bleeps). Synthwave style. Audio opt-in on first interaction (browser requirement).

## 4. Project Structure

```
app/
├── page.tsx                    # Title screen (New Game / Continue / Academy / About)

### Inventory

- Security Shield (HITL framework)

# Vibe Voyager — Design Document

> An interactive space exploration game that teaches vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering practices. From beginner to agentic developer.

**URL:** [REDACTED_DOMAIN]
**Hosting:** Vercel (free tier)
**Target:** Lecture demo + standalone learning platform
**Deadline:** ~2026-03-14

---

## 1. Audience

Mixed levels with multiple entry points:
- Software engineering students who code but haven't used AI tools
- Working developers adopting agentic workflows
- Beginners exploring AI-assisted development
- The Academy section is accessible without playing the game (direct access for anyone)

## 2. Narrative Arc

**Key narrative thread:** The game mirrors Karpathy's own evolution — he coined "vibe coding" (Feb 2025), then declared it "passé" and introduced **"agentic engineering"** (Feb 2026). The player lives this arc.

### Act 1 — "The Solo Pilot" (Beginner) — Vibe Coding
Player wakes as a rookie developer in a single-person ship. Learns to fly by talking to ship AI (vibe coding). Fast but fragile — tech debt accumulates. Confronts real 2026 data: AI code has 1.75x more bugs, 2.74x more XSS vulnerabilities. ARIA's key lesson: "Vibe coding got you here. Agentic engineering gets you to production."

### Act 2 — "First Contact" (Intermediate) — Agentic Engineering
Discovers MCP (agent-to-tool) and A2A (agent-to-agent) — the twin communication protocols. Learns agent architecture (Perceive → Plan → Act → Reflect). Recruits first crew members. Explores both third-party frameworks (CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen) AND official Agent SDKs (Claude, OpenAI, Google ADK).

### Act 3 — "Fleet Commander" (Advanced) — Production Mastery
Commands a fleet of specialized agent ships (multi-agent orchestration via A2A). Faces the Integration Nebula, deploys HITL safety systems, handles security threats including AI copyright/ethics. Final boss: deploying a production-grade agentic system.

### Epilogue — "The Academy" (Practitioner)
Ship docks at Fleet HQ. Unlocks real-world tooling guides. Space aesthetic continues, real-world content inside. Also accessible from title screen without game progress.

## 3. Tech Stack

| Dependency | Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Next.js | 15 (stable) | App Router, SSR/SSG, routing |
| TypeScript | latest | Type safety |
| Tailwind CSS | v4 | CSS-first config via `@import "tailwindcss"` and `@theme` |
| Motion | latest | Animations (`motion/react`, NOT framer-motion) |
| HTML5 Canvas | native | Star map, mini-games |
| Howler.js | latest | Audio (ambient loops + SFX sprites, 7kb gzipped) |
| localStorage | native | Game save state (no backend) |
| Vercel | free tier | Hosting + custom domain |

**No backend, no database, no auth.** All state client-side.

### Typography
- Display: Space Grotesk
- Body: Inter
- Mono: JetBrains Mono

### Color System
| Token | Hex | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| Void | `#0a0f1a` | Deep space background |
| Nebula Blue | `#4a6fa5` | Primary UI, MCP content |
| Signal Green | `#6b9e78` | Success, agent content, Plan/Act |
| Core Terracotta | `#c17147` | Warnings, highlights, player actions |
| Starlight | `#e8e0d4` | Text, glowing elements |
| Glass | `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)` | Glassmorphism panels with backdrop-blur |

### Visual Style
Clean minimalist sci-fi. Glassmorphism panels, parallax starfields, SVG planets with orbital rings, spring-physics animations, subtle glow effects. Think *Interstellar* UI meets Linear's design language.

### Audio
Full soundscape: ambient space synth loop + UI SFX (button clicks, warp sounds, mission complete chimes, dialogue bleeps). Synthwave style. Audio opt-in on first interaction (browser requirement).

## 4. Project Structure

```
app/
├── page.tsx                    # Title screen (New Game / Continue / Academy / About)
├── create/                     # Character creation (3 steps)
├── cockpit/                    # Ship HUD — main dashboard
├── starmap/                    # Interactive galaxy map (Canvas)
├── planets/
│   ├── vibe-world/            # Act 1: Vibe coding fundamentals
│   ├── debt-belt/             # Act 1: Tech debt dangers
│   ├── mcp-station/           # Act 2: Model Context Protocol
│   ├── agent-academy/         # Act 2: Agent architecture
│   ├── framework-nebula/      # Act 2: LangGraph vs CrewAI vs AutoGen
│   ├── orchestration-citadel/ # Act 3: Multi-agent systems
│   ├── security-fortress/     # Act 3: HITL, local LLMs, security
│   └── production-worlds/     # Act 3: Enterprise deployment
├── academy/                    # Epilogue: Real-world tooling guides
├── inventory/                  # Collected tools/items
└── crew/                       # Recruited agent crew

components/
├── game/
│   ├── StarMap.tsx             # Canvas-based galaxy navigation
│   ├── Cockpit.tsx             # HUD with stats, fuel, crew
│   ├── DialogueSystem.tsx      # NPC conversation engine
│   ├── MissionBriefing.tsx     # Mission intro/outro screens
│   ├── MiniGame.tsx            # Base mini-game wrapper
│   └── Inventory.tsx           # Item management UI
├── ui/
│   ├── GlassPanel.tsx          # Glassmorphism container
│   ├── XPBar.tsx               # Experience progress bar
│   ├── StatGauge.tsx           # Radial stat display
│   ├── TypewriterText.tsx      # Animated text reveal
│   └── WarpTransition.tsx      # Page transition effect
├── audio/
│   └── AudioManager.tsx        # Howler.js wrapper, SFX triggers

lib/
├── game-state.ts               # Save/load, progression logic
├── missions.ts                 # Mission definitions & requirements
├── dialogue-data.ts            # NPC conversation trees
├── items.ts                    # Item/tool definitions
└── crew.ts                     # Crew member definitions & stats

public/
├── audio/
│   ├── ambient-space.mp3
│   └── sfx/                    # UI sounds
├── images/
│   ├── planets/                # SVG/PNG planet illustrations
│   ├── characters/             # NPC portraits
│   ├── items/                  # Inventory icons
│   └── backgrounds/            # Starfields, nebulae
```

## 5. Game Systems

### Player Stats (4 stats, each 1–10)
| Stat | Represents | Leveled by |
|---|---|---|
| Vibe | Natural language fluency with AI | Vibe coding missions, prompt challenges |
| Architecture | System design & agent thinking | Agent anatomy, framework comparisons |
| Protocol | Integration & MCP knowledge | MCP missions, connection challenges |
| Command | Leadership of multi-agent systems | Orchestration missions, fleet exercises |

### Ranks (combined stat total)
| Rank | Total | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| Cadet | 4–10 | Act 1 |
| Navigator | 11–20 | Act 2 |
| Commander | 21–30 | Act 3 |
| Admiral | 31–40 | Academy (also accessible from title screen) |

### Character Creation
1. Choose callsign (text input)
2. Choose ship (3 cosmetic SVG silhouettes: The Spark, The Architect, The Sentinel)
3. Intro text crawl → [ LAUNCH ] → warp into cockpit

### Mission Structure
Each planet has 3–5 missions. Each mission follows: **Briefing → Learning Phase → Challenge → Debrief**

### Challenge Types
| Type | Mechanic |
|---|---|
| Prompt Duel | Write best natural language prompt, scored on completeness |
| Architect | Drag-and-drop nodes to build system diagrams |
| Connect | Draw connections in visual puzzle (MCP wiring) |
| Debug | Find problems in code/architecture scenarios |
| Command | Assign right agents to right tasks |
| Dialogue | NPC quiz-conversations with branching answers |

### Crew System (maps to Perceive → Plan → Act → Reflect)
| Member | Role | Recruited at |
|---|---|---|
| ARIA | Ship AI / narrator | Start of game |
| Scout | Perception specialist | Agent Academy M1 |
| Archie | Planning / reasoning | Agent Academy M3 |
| Exec | Action / execution | Agent Academy M5 |
| Mirror | Reflection / testing | Security Fortress M1 |

### Inventory
Items = real tools with in-game names. Each has a description card explaining the real-world tool.
- Ship Voice Module (Claude Code / Cursor)
- Context Adapter (MCP)
- Agent Blueprint (Agent architecture pattern)
- Fleet Comm Array (Multi-agent orchestration)
- Security Shield (HITL framework)
- Local Core (Ollama / Local LLMs)
- Skill Chips (Claude Code skills/plugins)

### Save System
- Auto-save to localStorage after every mission
- No password gating — progression earned through completion
- "New Game" reset option

## 6. Planet-by-Planet Content Map

### ACT 1 — "The Solo Pilot"

**Vibe World** (4 missions)
1. "First Words" — What is vibe coding → Dialogue quiz (sources: IBM, Replit, Wikipedia, Google Cloud)
2. "See It, Say It, Run It" — First vibe creation → Prompt Duel (sources: Slide 2, Beginner Guide)
3. "The Prototype Sprint" — Build fast → Timed challenge (source: arXiv Vibe Coding in Practice)
4. "Traditional vs. Vibe" — Both paradigms → Debate dialogue (source: arXiv GenAI & Software Dev)

**Debt Asteroid Belt** (4 missions)
1. "The Fragile Ship" — Tech debt → Debug 5 problems (sources: Slide 9, Tabnine)
2. "The Quality Crisis" — 2026 data: 1.75x more bugs, 2.74x more XSS, 4x more code cloning → Debug real vulnerability types (sources: CodeRabbit report, Black Duck OSSRA 2026)
3. "Your Career in the AI Era" — Harvard study: junior dev employment drops 9-10%, BUT AI unlocks new domains → Dialogue with career counselor NPC (sources: Harvard study, Stack Overflow)
4. "The Case for Expertise" — Why vibe alone isn't enough, transition to agentic engineering → Dialogue quiz, Karpathy quote, unlocks Act 2

### ACT 2 — "First Contact"

**MCP Station** (5 missions)
1. "The N×M Problem" — Integration bottleneck → Visual puzzle (source: Slide 4)
2. "USB-C for AI" — What MCP is, 97M monthly downloads, Linux Foundation governance → Connect puzzle (sources: Slide 5, Anthropic, IBM, Context Studios)
3. "Protocol vs. Wrappers" — Comparison, MCP 1.0 targeting June 2026 → Dialogue quiz (source: Slide 6)
4. "Docking Sequence" — MCP hands-on config → Architect JSON blocks (source: Anthropic docs)
5. "The Babel Problem" — Intro to A2A: agents can use tools (MCP) but can't talk to each other. Discovery of Agent-to-Agent protocol → Connect puzzle wiring agents together (sources: Google A2A blog, Linux Foundation)

**Agent Academy** (5 missions)
1. "The Cognitive Loop" — Agent anatomy → Architect cycle + recruit Scout (source: Slide 3)
2. "Perception Training" — How agents see → Sorting mini-game (source: arXiv)
3. "Planning & Reasoning" — Chain of thought → Tree decomposition + recruit Archie (source: Deep Agent article)
4. "Tool Calling" — How agents act → Connect puzzle (sources: Akka, ACI)
5. "Self-Healing" — Reflect loop → Debug scenarios + recruit Exec (source: Slide 3)

**Framework Nebula** (5 missions)
1. "Three Schools of Thought" — Framework overview: LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen → NPC dialogues (source: Slide 8, DataCamp)
2. "The Official Armories" — Vendor Agent SDKs: Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK → Comparison dialogue + Architect (sources: Anthropic docs, OpenAI docs, Google ADK docs)
3. "The Right Tool" — When to use what (frameworks vs SDKs vs custom) → Command matching (source: DataCamp, ClickHouse comparison)
4. "Build a Crew" — CrewAI concepts → Architect fill-in-blank (sources: CrewAI, CAMEL repos)
5. "Agent Cards" — A2A capability discovery, AGENTS.md configuration → Architect: build an Agent Card JSON (sources: A2A protocol docs, AGENTS.md spec)

### ACT 3 — "Fleet Commander"

**Orchestration Citadel** (4 missions)
1. "Society of Agents" — Multi-agent pipeline → Architect nodes (source: Slide 7)
2. "The A2A Network" — A2A protocol deep dive: capability discovery, task delegation, artifact exchange between agents. 72% of enterprise projects now use multi-agent architectures → Connect routing with Agent Cards (sources: Google A2A blog, FrankX roadmap)
3. "Message Passing" — Agent communication patterns → Connect routing (sources: arXiv, Devin blog)
4. "Delegation" — What to automate (87% of Fortune 500 use AI coding tools) → Command triage (sources: arXiv, Second Talent stats)

**Security Fortress** (4 missions)
1. "The Safety Net" — HITL → Architect flowchart + recruit Mirror (sources: Slide 10, Galileo)
2. "Local Defenses" — Local LLMs → Dialogue quiz (source: Slide 11)
3. "Threat Scan" — Security vulnerabilities → Debug challenge (sources: Auto Fixer, CWE-95, Black Duck OSSRA 2026)
4. "The Legal Frontier" — AI copyright, licensing, open-source attribution, disclosure rules. Mirror raises the concerns → Dialogue quiz (sources: U.S. Copyright Office, Red Hat legal analysis)

**Production Worlds** (3 missions — three moons)
1. "Moon Alpha: Quality Engineering" — Self-healing tests → Command (sources: Slide 12, SWE-bench)
2. "Moon Beta: The Enterprise" — Real-world cases → Dialogue quiz (source: Slides 12-13)
3. "Final Mission: Deployment Playbook" — Capstone → Multi-step Architect (sources: Slides 14-15)

## 7. The Academy (Epilogue + Direct Access)

Accessible from title screen without game progress. Space aesthetic continues, real-world content inside glassmorphism panels with terminal-style code blocks.

### Section 1: AI-Powered IDEs & Editors

#### GUI-Based IDEs
| Tool | Developer | Key Differentiator | Pricing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cursor** | Anysphere | Largest community, highest benchmark scores, tab completions + agent mode | $20/mo Pro |
| **Google Antigravity** | Google | Agent-first platform, Manager Surface for multi-agent orchestration, built-in browser testing | Free preview |
| **Kiro** | AWS | Spec-driven development, Agent Hooks for automation, Agent Steering docs | Free preview |
| **Windsurf** | Cognition (Devin) | Cascade agent anticipates next moves, best value at $15/mo | $15/mo Pro |
| **GitHub Copilot** | GitHub/Microsoft | Deepest GitHub integration, workspace agents, code review built-in | $10/mo |

#### Terminal-Native Agents
| Tool | Developer | Key Differentiator | Pricing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code** | Anthropic | 1M token context, deepest reasoning, skills/plugins/hooks ecosystem | $20/mo Pro, $100-200/mo Teams |
| **Codex CLI** | OpenAI | Rust-built, multi-agent with worktrees, MCP support, open source | Usage-based |
| **Gemini CLI** | Google | 1M token context, free tier (60 req/min), Google Search grounding, open source (Apache 2.0) | Free / usage-based |
| **Aider** | Paul Gauthier | Speed-focused, multi-file changes via natural language, git-aware, open source | Free (OSS) |

#### VS Code Extensions (Open Source)
| Tool | Key Differentiator |
|---|---|
| **Cline** | Model-agnostic, stepwise Plan→Act pipeline, full audit trail, governance-focused |
| **Roo Code** | Cline fork, role-driven execution modes (architect/tester), faster on large multi-file changes |
| **Continue** | Open-source autopilot, source-controlled AI checks on PRs |

### Section 2: AI Code Review & Quality Tools

| Tool | What It Does |
|---|---|
| **CodeRabbit** | AI PR reviewer on GitHub/GitLab, 2M+ repos connected, auto-summaries and walkthroughs |
| **Greptile** | Full-codebase graph analysis for cross-file bug detection |
| **Qodo** | Behavior-focused review, auto-generates test suites, persistent codebase intelligence |
| **Ellipsis** | Auto-generates fixes for reviewer comments, reduces review cycles |
| **Cursor BugBot** | Automated bug detection integrated into Cursor IDE |

### Section 3: No-Code / Low-Code Builders

| Tool | What It Does |
|---|---|
| **Replit** | Browser-based IDE with AI agent, deploy in one click |
| **Bolt.new** | Prompt-to-app builder, full-stack in browser |
| **Lovable** | AI app builder focused on design quality |
| **v0 by Vercel** | UI component generator from prompts, React + Tailwind output |

### Section 4: Claude Code Deep Dive
- Installation & setup
- CLAUDE.md configuration (global vs. project vs. local)
- Skills: what they are, how to create and use them
- Plugins: installing from marketplaces, compound-engineering, superpowers
- Hooks: pre/post tool call automation
- Agent teams: parallel execution with subagents
- Keybindings & keyboard shortcuts
- MCP server configuration
- Best practices: brainstorming → planning → execution → review cycle

### Section 5: Agentic Development Best Practices
- Subagent-driven development (5-step workflow)
- When to parallelize vs. serialize
- Code review with AI (using multiple reviewer agents)
- Test-driven development with agents
- Memory management (CLAUDE.md, memory files, progressive disclosure)
- Security: HITL patterns, sandboxing, local LLMs
- Prompt engineering for code generation
- Managing technical debt in AI-assisted codebases

### Section 6: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Workshop
- What MCP is and why it matters (from game content, reinforced with hands-on)
- Setting up MCP servers (stdio vs. HTTP)
- Connecting Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI to MCP
- Building your own MCP server
- MCP in enterprise: governance and scaling

### Section 7: Resource Library
All 57+ sources from sources.md, organized by topic with description cards.
Links to arXiv papers, corporate articles, GitHub repos, benchmarks.

### Section 8: How This Was Built
Meta case study from BUILD_LOG.md:
- The brainstorming process
- Planning with skills
- Parallel agent execution (what ran concurrently)
- Plugins & skills used
- Metrics (lines of code, time, agent count)
- Lessons learned

## 8. UX Flow

### Title Screen
Slow-drifting parallax starfield. Nebula gradient pulses gently.

```
         V I B E   V O Y A G E R
         The Agentic Coding Odyssey

         [  N E W   G A M E  ]
         [  C O N T I N U E  ]
         [  A C A D E M Y    ]
         [  A B O U T        ]
```

- Ambient audio starts on first interaction
- "Continue" grayed out if no save exists
- "Academy" always accessible (no game progress required)

### Core Navigation Loop
```
Star Map ──select planet──→ Planet (missions) ──complete/return──→ Cockpit (HUD home)
   ↑                                                                      │
   └──────────────────────── open star map ───────────────────────────────┘
```

### Persistent Nav Bar (bottom, cockpit-styled)
Star Map | Cockpit (home) | Crew | Inventory | Academy | Audio Toggle

### Star Map (Canvas)
- 3-layer parallax starfield
- Planets as glowing spheres with orbital ring animations
- 3 visible regions: Act 1 (warm, center), Act 2 (cool, frontier), Act 3 (dramatic, edge)
- Academy space station always visible at top
- Planet states: Locked (dim) → Available (pulsing) → In Progress (partial ring) → Completed (full glow + badge)

### Cockpit HUD
Glassmorphism panels on starfield:
- Callsign + Rank
- 4 stat gauges (radial/horizontal bars with glow)
- Crew portraits (silhouette with "?" for unrecruited)
- Mission log (current objective + overall progress)
- Recent inventory items

### Page Transitions
- Star Map → Planet: Stars streak toward center (warp in)
- Planet → Cockpit: Gentle fade with HUD boot-up flicker
- Cockpit → Star Map: Reverse warp (stars expand outward)
- Mission complete: Flash of light → debrief slides in
- All via Motion `AnimatePresence` with custom variants

### Mobile Responsiveness
- Star map: scrollable/zoomable touch canvas
- Cockpit: stacks vertically
- Dialogue: already mobile-friendly (text + buttons)
- Mini-games: tap instead of click/drag
- Nav bar: fixed bottom (thumb-friendly)

## 9. Content Gaps to Create

| Gap | Location | Source |
|---|---|---|
| AI tools landscape (IDEs, agents, review tools) | Academy Sections 1-3 | Research + first-hand experience |
| Claude Code deep dive tutorials | Academy Section 4 | Written from experience |
| Agentic best practices guide | Academy Section 5 | [redacted-project]/Continuum workflows |
| MCP setup walkthrough | Academy Section 6 | Anthropic docs |
| Mini-game interactive content | All challenge missions | Built as game mechanics |
| NPC dialogue scripts | All planets | Written from source material |
| Audio assets | Global | Royalty-free / generated |
| Planet/character SVG illustrations | Global | AI-generated or designed |

## 10. Build Approach

- **Framework:** Superpowers plugin workflow (brainstorm → plan → execute → review)
- **Execution:** Subagent-driven development with parallel agent teams
- **Quality:** Compound engineering review agents between phases
- **Tracking:** BUILD_LOG.md updated after every major milestone
- **Verification:** verification-before-completion skill before any "done" claim
- **Docs:** Context7 for all library API verification before writing code
